source.note: Facts from the friction-audit research; (U) entries are unverified and have needs_research=true.

edr.note: Vendor EDR process names are not yet researched.

actions.problem: Spotlight indexes worktrees and build output

detect.text: `mds`, `mds_stores` or `mdworker` appear in the busiest processes; `mdutil -s <volume>` reports indexing enabled (volume level only, no root); the folder has no `.noindex` ancestor.

steps: System Settings > Spotlight > Search Privacy: add the worktree parent folder with the + button (no admin needed for folders you own).
Or create new worktrees under a parent folder whose name ends in `.noindex`. This moves paths, so it is only ever proposed.

verify.note: The Search Privacy list cannot be read without root. Check that the folder has a `.noindex` ancestor, or that `mds` drops out of the busiest processes.

actions.undo: Remove the folder from the Search Privacy list.

actions.problem: Time Machine backs up churning build output

detect.text: `backupd` appears in the busiest processes; `tmutil isexcluded <path>` prints `[Included]` for a regenerable output folder.

steps: Run `tmutil addexclusion <path>` for each regenerable output folder (a sticky exclusion, no root; never use `-p`).
flap_steps: The sticky exclusion is lost when a clean build recreates the folder. Ask the user to run a fixed-path exclusion for the folder (`sudo tmutil addexclusion -p <path>`, needs root and Full Disk Access for the terminal app), or to move build output to a parent folder outside backups. (Unverified: that `-p` survives recreation.)

actions.problem: Time Machine local snapshots hold disk space

detect.text: Free space is low and `tmutil listlocalsnapshots /` lists snapshots.

steps: In System Settings, turn automatic backups off, wait, then turn them on again. Apple says this is how local snapshots are removed. This deletes those local restore points, and turning backups on again does not bring them back.

verify.note: Re-run host-probe and check free disk space.

actions.problem: Defender scans the repo and the toolchain

detect.text: `MsMpEng` or `MpDefenderCoreService` present. Informational: only an action when slow calls or a regression fired in the same project. Exclusions cannot be read without admin by default.

steps: As administrator, run `Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath <path>`, or add the folder in Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Exclusions.
Or create a new Dev Drive (admin; existing volumes cannot be converted). Keep real-time protection on.

verify.note: Reading exclusions needs admin: run `Get-MpPreference` as administrator.

actions.undo: Remove the exclusion with `Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath <path>` as administrator.

steps: Settings > Privacy & security > Searching Windows > Add an excluded folder.

verify.note: Check the excluded folders list on the same page.

actions.undo: Remove the folder from the excluded list.

detect.text: `localsearch*` or `tracker-miner-fs-3` in the busiest processes; `localsearch status`.

steps: Create an empty `.nomedia` file in the output folder (LocalSearch skips folders that contain it).
System Settings > File Search: set the folder to Not indexed.

verify.note: Run `balooctl status` and check the folder list.

actions.undo: Set the folder back to Indexed.

actions.problem: File watchers fail because the inotify limits are too low

detect.text: `max_user_watches` is below twice the tracked file count; or tools report 'No space left on device' while the disk has room, 'upper limit on inotify watches reached' or 'User limit of inotify instances reached'.

steps: Run `sudo sysctl fs.inotify.max_user_watches=<n>` and persist it in a file under `/etc/sysctl.d/` (needs root). Reading the limits needs no root.

verify.note: A value of 100000 or more is a heuristic.

actions.undo: Set the previous value back with sysctl.

actions.problem: Third-party antivirus or EDR scans agent output

detect.text: A catalogued antivirus process is busy (only ClamAV names are catalogued so far).

verify.note: Only IT can confirm the exclusion.

actions.undo: Ask IT to remove the exclusion.

actions.problem: The repo sits inside iCloud, OneDrive, Dropbox or Google Drive

detect.text: An ancestor folder of the project matches a cloud-sync folder name.

steps: Move the repo to a local folder outside the synced folders (for example `~/Developer`) and re-clone or move it there.

detect.text: `/proc/version` mentions Microsoft and the project path starts with `/mnt/`.
More than 8 worktrees or more than 10 GB of regenerable output, and some linked worktrees are clean, merged and unlocked.

steps: Run `worktree-prune apply --project <repo> --path <worktree>` (it removes the worktree without `--force` and keeps the branch), or `git worktree remove <path>` yourself.
actions.undo: Run `git worktree add <path> <branch>` (the branch was kept).

actions.problem: Stale worktrees that are dirty, unmerged or locked

detect.text: Linked worktrees with no commit in 14 days that are not safe to remove automatically.

steps: Decide per worktree: merge or push the branch, then remove it; or commit or discard the changes.

actions.problem: Free disk space is low on the repo volume

detect.text: Free space on the repo volume is under 10% or under 20 GB.

steps: Remove regenerable build output you no longer need (the probe lists the git-ignored output folders and their sizes).
